meaning.en: To destroy (land and buildings) by fire or military action so as to leave nothing salvageable to an enemy army.

sentences.en: Those two issues can sometimes melt or scorch an area around the batteries, rendering the phone inoperable.

sentences.en: That tends to be gentler than the hotter afternoon sun and your plants will be less likely to scorch.

sentences.en: Heat/Fire Resistant - With a ceramic tiles countertop, you can take the pot right off the oven and place it directly on the tile; the tile won't scorch or emit toxic fumes.

sentences.en: Apply water directly to the soil in the mornings to prevent leaf scorch.

sentences.en: The foliage is best in partial shade - the delicate variegated leaves may scorch in full sun.

sentences.en: Up to 60% of plants prefer these cool, sun scorch free, permanently moist sites.

sentences.en: They will hold their arms over their heads until the muscles atrophy, will keep their fists clenched till the nails grow through the palms, will lie on beds of nails, cut and stab themselves, drag, week after week, enormous chains loaded with masses of iron, or hang themselves before a fire near enough to scorch.
sentences.vi: Họ sẽ ôm tay qua đầu cho đến khi cơ bắp teo đi, sẽ nắm chặt tay cho đến khi móng tay mọc xuyên qua lòng bàn tay, sẽ nằm trên giường đinh, cắt và tự đâm, kéo lê, tuần này qua tuần khác, những sợi xích khổng lồ chất đầy sắt, hoặc treo cổ mình trước ngọn lửa đủ gần để thiêu đốt.

sentences.en: The Danehill Dancer filly made all in thrilling style to scorch to a two-and-a-half length victory in the fillies ' Classic.
